name: Reverse Buggy Choke
description: A choke from bottom side control where you wrap your legs around the opponent's neck and arm — a lower-percentage attack that should not replace fundamental frames and hip escapes.
shortInstruction: Wrap legs around their neck and arm, squeeze — the reverse buggy is a desperation attack from bottom side control.
summary: The reverse buggy choke is a variation of the buggy choke from bottom side control. The key difference is the leg positioning — in the reverse buggy, your legs wrap around their neck and one arm from the opposite side. Like the standard buggy choke, it is a surprise attack rather than a primary strategy. It works best against opponents who pressure heavily with a crossface, leaving their neck exposed on the other side.
whyItWorks: The element of surprise — opponents do not expect a choke from bottom side control.
Can catch opponents who are heavy on the crossface side, exposing their neck.
Creates a momentary dilemma — defend the choke or maintain side control.
Useful as a last-resort attack when conventional escapes are failing.
commonMistakes: Using it as a primary escape instead of frames and hip escapes.
Leaving the underhook available — the underhook is more important than the choke.
Letting the opponent stack you — this neutralizes the choke and puts you in danger.
Wasting energy on the choke when you could be escaping to a better position.
coachingCues: If they stack you, release immediately.
Underhook first, then attack — never the other way.
One attempt — if it fails, return to fundamentals.
safetySummary: The reverse buggy choke compresses the neck — apply gradually and release on tap.
Do not use against larger opponents who can stack you — the stack can injure your lower back.
Tap early if you feel the choke is being applied to your own neck.
keyCorrections: If they stack you, you committed too early or at the wrong angle — release and reset to frames.
If they pull their arm free, your leg wrap was too loose — wrap tighter or abandon the choke.
If you can't finish, return to conventional side control escapes (hip escape, underhook).

systemLogic.corePrinciple: Bottom side control: opponent is heavy on crossface side → wrap legs around their neck and arm → squeeze → choke.

decisionTree.action: The reverse buggy is a tertiary option — frames and hip escapes are primary.
go to hip escape and underhook recovery.

moneyDetails: The leg wrap must include their neck AND one arm — wrapping only the neck will not secure the choke.
Keep your top leg over their back to prevent them from pulling out of the wrap.
The choke comes from squeezing your thighs together — not from pulling with your legs.
If they posture up, the choke is lost — immediately return to frames and hip escape.
nextStep: After understanding the reverse buggy choke, focus on primary side control escapes: frames, hip escape, and underhook recovery.
fixItFast: They stack you? Release and frame on their hips.
Legs slipping off? Wrap tighter around their arm.
Can't get the choke? Return to frames and hip escape.
